grammar_rules.name: Quotative Marker Agreement
grammar_rules.description: The quotative marker (the particle introducing direct or reported speech) must agree with the subject prefix of the reporting verb.
grammar_rules.rule: Subject prefix determines the quotative marker: n- (1sg) -> nti; u- (2sg) -> uti; a- (3sg) -> ati; tu- (1pl) -> tuti; mu- (2pl) -> muti; ba- (3pl) -> bati.

incorrect.error: Singular quotative ('ati') used with plural subject prefix ('ba-')
Singular quotative ('ati') used with plural subject prefix ('tu-')

grammar_rules.name: Temporal reference: ejo / ejo bundi
grammar_rules.description: 'Ejo' means both 'yesterday' and 'tomorrow'; accompanying words resolve the direction. 'Ejo bundi' extends the same neutrality two days out.
grammar_rules.rule: The word 'ejo' is temporally neutral and can refer to the past or the future; context, tense, or an accompanying word disambiguates it. 'Ejo hashize' ('hashize' = the past) means 'yesterday'. 'Ejo hazaza' ('hazaza' = the future) means 'tomorrow'. 'Ejo bundi' shifts one day further out and stays neutral like 'ejo': 'ejo bundi (hashize)' means 'the day before yesterday' and 'ejo bundi (hazaza)' means 'the day after tomorrow'.

incorrect.error: 'ejo bundi' refers to two days out (before or after), not to 'yesterday'; 'yesterday' is 'ejo hashize'

lexical_exceptions.rule: This noun has no plural form. The form *amakwe (formed by analogy with class 6 ama-) is not valid in standard Kinyarwanda.

lexical_exceptions.rule: Must be written as two words when 'ni' functions as the copula ('it is'). The contraction 'n'ukuri' is valid only when 'n'' represents 'na' (and / with), not when it represents the copula 'ni'.

correct.translation: It is true that he came
correct.note: 'ni' is the copula 'it is' — must be separated from 'ukuri'
'n'' is a contraction of 'na' (and) — contraction is valid here

incorrect.error: Missing space — the copula 'ni' must be separated from 'ukuri'
Wrong contraction — the copula 'ni' should not be contracted to 'n'' here
